- "Period: Jan 1, 2025 — Dec 31, 2025" is intended to be inclusive of the full day on Dec 31, 2025. In practice we treat the period end as 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC for evidence exports, but Soojin will confirm the canonical timestamp we use.

- Bridge letters are available on request — they require coordination with our audit firm and typically take 3-10 business days depending on the scope. Marissa can advise on standard wording and process.

Hi Sarah — thanks for the detailed ask, and hi team. I'm providing more technical detail so your auditors can map controls to artifacts. Short answers first, then examples: 

1) Period inclusivity
- We consider the report period inclusive through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. All timestamped exports we provide will use UTC by default; if your auditor needs a different timezone we can annotate.

2) Point-in-time evidence types we can provide
- IAM / account lists: CSV export of active accounts/roles as-of the requested timestamp (snapshot taken from access management system).
- Token revocation / session events: event stream export from auth service filtered to an exact timestamp window (supports up to millisecond resolution).
- KMS / encryption: key metadata and rotation history with timestamps; configuration snapshot as-of date.
- Configuration / infrastructure: Terraform state or control-plane config snapshots and change history; where we cannot share code, we provide rendered config exports.
- Vulnerability and patching: sampled scan results and remediation tickets within the period (vuln mgmt is sampled by auditors; we provide the ticketing history for the sample).

3) Limitations / expectations
- For some third-party hosted services we only have provider-supplied attestations; we'll flag those in the checklist.
- If the auditor requires proof that no material changes occurred between the report end and a later date, we need to prepare a bridge letter. The bridge letter states there were no material changes in controls and will be reviewed/approved by the auditor — plan for a 3-10 business-day turnaround including auditor sign-off.

Next steps I propose:
- Sarah: confirm the exact as-of timestamp you want for each control type (e.g., 2025-12-31T23:59:59Z for IAM; a 48-hour window for token logs if you need a tolerance).
- Once confirmed, we'll produce a short evidence matrix mapping each auditor item to an artifact and upload to a secure folder.

I've attached a short text file with instructions for exporting log slices and preferred file formats (log-export-instructions.txt).

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
